summary: Retrieval score calibration: length-normalize vector similarity + hub-frequency dampening to counter the fluency inversion (modern-synthesis prose out-scoring archaic primaries). Score-time fix (vs the emit-time per-work cap). Sweep each against the frozen golden gate; no regression below 316/4. Targets pistis-sophia (rank 19 no crowder) + deep-crowding iamblichus/mabinogion. See docs/retrieval-golden-gap-investigation.md §8.1.
description:
BLIND-PICKUP START: read docs/retrieval-golden-gap-investigation.md end to end first (esp. §9 cold-start guide: prereqs, gate command, the measurement-harness recipe, env knobs), then establish the 316/4 baseline before changing anything.

GOAL: counter the fluency inversion — modern-synthesis prose (blavatsky-sd et al.) out-scoring archaic primaries (§5). Score-TIME fix, distinct from the emit-time per-work cap (§6, which only removes duplicates and can't lift a buried primary).

TWO independent sub-experiments (§8.1), each swept against the frozen 320-probe gate:
  1. length-normalize the vector similarity term (stop rewarding verbose prose)
  2. hub-frequency dampening — discount a work by how often it matches across UNRELATED queries (blavatsky held 18-32 of the top scored slots, §5)

SHIP GATE: no regression below 316/4 (a scoring change touches every query — run the FULL gate, not a spot check). Add a new env knob defaulting to current behaviour (redeploy-free rollback), like RETRIEVAL_GRAPH_RANK/MAX_PER_TEXT.
TARGETS: pistis-sophia (rank 19, no crowder — pure scoring) + deep-crowding iamblichus (rank 48; but first rule out the 6e0c2a63 apparatus-contamination confound on iamblichus .162-.180) / mabinogion (rank 25, loses to Kalevala — a genuine parallel myth, may be unwinnable).
NOT this ticket: extractConcepts upgrade (todo:53480da1, §8.2), candidate-generation recall for isa-upanishad which never enters the pool (§8.3), thin-tradition safety (todo:31a7fe76, §8.4).

analysis.author: Backend Engineer
analysis.content: Both §8.1 levers built as env-gated knobs (default OFF, vector-similarity-term only) and swept against the full gate. Baseline at true defaults = 314/6 (the doc's 316/4 is the cap=1 figure, not the shipped default). Results: RETRIEVAL_LENGTH_NORM=0.5 -> 301/19 (-13: recovers iamblichus 48->5 but BM25's symmetric short-boost floods short-text precision — dhammapada/sutras/pythagorean/gathas); RETRIEVAL_HUB_DAMPEN=0.15 -> 306/14 (-8: centroid-proximity conflates omnibus crowders with broad primaries — iamblichus is centrality-rank 9/246 — so it dampens targets, knocking out yoga-sutras/tao-te-ching/plotinus/gospel-of-thomas). Neither beats baseline; both ship OFF (defaults unchanged, gate stays 314/6). These two FORMULATIONS do not fix the fluency inversion. Reformulation paths (one-sided long-only length penalty; literal cross-query hit-frequency excluding on-topic queries) recorded in docs §8.1. The residual 4 (iamblichus/isa/mabinogion/pistis) now point harder at §8.2 (extractConcepts) and §8.3 (recall) than at vector-score calibration. Committed 59737d3.

analysis.author: Backend Engineer
analysis.content: SUPERSEDES the ship-OFF note: owner's call is that dead env machinery is net-negative, so the two calibration levers were REVERTED (not shipped even off). Kept: the measurement (both regress — length 301/19, hub 306/14 vs 314/6) and the redirect. Real lever = a curated MODERN-SYNTHESIS dampen keyed on tradition/era, NOT any vector-score transform. Era is orthogonal to the embedding's semantic axis (modern+ancient same-topic passages are neighbours), which is why length (verbosity != era) and centrality (breadth != era; iamblichus is central rank 9/246) both regressed. tradition is a clean proxy: dampen {theosophy, western_esoteric} (+ renaissance_hermeticism at half weight) — hits the actual crowders (blavatsky, secret-teachings), touches none of the ancient targets. No composition-date column exists (works/ work_dossiers prose only), so a finer per-work era is a guru-repo corpus-export addition. Ticket stays OPEN, re-pointed at the era lever. See docs §8.1.
